claims.claim: Expands the 'dangerous crime' and 'crime of violence' definitions
claims.sourceSpan:
by striking ``Burglary or
attempted burglary'' and inserting ``Burglary in the first

claims.note: DIRECTION INVERSION. Source strikes broad "Burglary or attempted burglary" / "Robbery or attempted robbery" and inserts the NARROWER "Burglary in the first degree, attempted burglary in the first degree, or burglary with a dangerous weapon" (same for robbery, and in the crime-of-violence definition). The set of qualifying burglaries/robberies SHRINKS to a strict subset — a narrowing, not an expansion. Lesser burglary/robbery is moved into the new "public safety or order crime" (cash-bail) bucket.

claims.claim: The definitions of 'dangerous crime' and 'crime of violence' are expanded to include first-degree burglary and robbery, attempts, and those committed with a dangerous weapon
claims.sourceSpan:
by striking ``Burglary or
attempted burglary'' and inserting ``Burglary in the first
degree, attempted burglary in the first degree, or burglary
with a dangerous weapon''
claims.note: DIRECTION INVERSION + false "to include". The definitions are NARROWED, not expanded: source strikes the broad "Burglary or attempted burglary"/"Robbery or attempted robbery" and inserts only first-degree/attempted-first-degree/dangerous-weapon variants. First-degree burglary and robbery were already covered under the broad terms, so they are not newly "included"; rather, ordinary (non-first-degree, non-armed) burglary/robbery is REMOVED from these definitions.
